title: DeepResearch Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Deep Research Agents

key_points.claim: Benchmark of 100 PhD-level expert-crafted research tasks across 22 fields for evaluating deep research agents.
key_points.evidence_quote: a benchmark consisting of 100 PhD-level research tasks, each meticulously crafted by domain experts across 22 distinct fields

key_points.claim: Proposes a reference-based method with adaptive criteria to assess report quality, aligned with human judgment.
key_points.evidence_quote: a reference-based method with adaptive criteria to assess the quality of generated research reports

key_points.claim: Separately evaluates retrieval/collection via effective citation count and citation accuracy.
key_points.evidence_quote: evaluate DRA's information retrieval and collection capabilities by assessing its effective citation count and overall citation accuracy

key_points.claim: Evaluating DRAs is hard and labor-intensive, motivating automated methods validated against human judgment.
key_points.evidence_quote: Evaluating DRAs is inherently complex and labor-intensive.

key_points.claim: Code and key components are open-sourced.
key_points.evidence_quote: We have open-sourced DeepResearch Bench and key components of these frameworks

reliability_notes: Abstract page only (not full paper), so no numeric results. Peer-review status unknown; preprint by the benchmark authors, who may favor their own method.
